Consider the diagram shown above, where $\overset{\to }{QT}=a,$ $\overset{\to }{RS}=b,$ $\overset{\to }{TR}=c,$ and $\overset{\to }{RP}=d.$ Find $\overset{\to }{QS}$ in terms of $a,b,c,$ and $d.$
feedback.worked_solution:
We want to find a "path" from $Q$ to $S$ consisting only of the vectors $a,b,c,$ and $d.$

According to the triangle law of addition,

$$
\overset{\to }{QS}=\overset{\to }{QT}+\overset{\to }{TR}+\overset{\to }{RS}
$$

as shown below.

![](/home/jake/Developer/Course_Academy/reference/mathacademy/question-capture-workers/linear/14040990/assets/2297c60ae34a641e498aa41346778e327fd2286657914272088ddb9f9b03bcb7.png)

  

Now, from the original diagram, we have that

$$
\overset{\to }{QT}=a,\,\overset{\to }{TR}=c,\,\overset{\to }{RS}=b.
$$

Let's add these to our diagram.

![](/home/jake/Developer/Course_Academy/reference/mathacademy/question-capture-workers/linear/14040990/assets/fb4850a7d309448213c1ac5572dfe112555a2938790b24fad03ebb4669e3d95a.png)

Therefore, we obtain

$$
\begin{aligned}\overset{\to }{QS} & =\overset{\to }{QT}+\overset{\to }{TR}+\overset{\to }{RS} \\  & =a+c+b.\end{aligned}
$$
